sanskrit: pratiprayāte dāśārṇe pārthive hemavarmaṇi kanyaivāhaṃ bhaviṣyāmi puruṣas tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi
english: When the Dāśārṇa king Hemavarman has gone back again, I shall become a maiden once more, and you shall become a man.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktvā samayaṃ tatra cakrāte tāv ubhau nṛpa anyonyasyānabhidrohe tau saṃkrāmayatāṃ tataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus, the two of them, O king, made a pact there—that they would do no harm to one another—and then they exchanged their forms.

sanskrit: strīliṅgaṃ dhārayām āsa sthūṇo yakṣo narādhipa yakṣarūpaṃ ca tad dīptaṃ śikhaṇḍī pratyapadyata
english: The yakṣa Sthūṇa took on the female sign, O lord of men, and Śikhaṇḍin received that blazing form of the yakṣa.

sanskrit: tataḥ śikhaṇḍī pāñcālyaḥ puṃstvam āsādya pārthiva viveśa nagaraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ pitaraṃ ca samāsadat yathāvṛttaṃ tu tat sarvam ācakhyau drupadasya ca
english: Then Śikhaṇḍin of the Pāñcālas, having attained manhood, O king, entered the city rejoicing, came to his father, and recounted to Drupada all that had befallen, just as it had happened.

sanskrit: drupadas tasya tac chrutvā harṣam āhārayat param sabhāryas tac ca sasmāra maheśvaravacas tadā
english: When Drupada heard this from him, he conceived the greatest joy, and together with his wife he then called to mind the words of Maheśvara.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpreṣayām āsa daśārṇādhipater nṛpa puruṣo 'yaṃ mama sutaḥ śraddhattāṃ me bhavān iti
english: Then he sent word to the lord of the Daśārṇas, O king: "This son of mine is a man—let your honour believe me in this."

sanskrit: atha dāśārṇako rājā sahasābhyāgamat tadā pāñcālarājaṃ drupadaṃ duḥkhāmarṣasamanvitaḥ
english: Thereupon the Dāśārṇa king came at once against Drupada, the king of the Pāñcālas, filled with grief and indignation.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāmpilyam āsādya daśārṇādhipatis tadā preṣayām āsa satkṛtya dūtaṃ brahmavidāṃ varam
english: Then, having reached Kāmpilya, the lord of the Daśārṇas, with due honour, dispatched as his envoy the foremost of those learned in the Veda.

sanskrit: brūhi madvacanād dūta pāñcālyaṃ taṃ nṛpādhamam yad vai kanyāṃ svakanyārthe vṛtavān asi durmate phalaṃ tasyāvalepasya drakṣyasy adya na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Say in my name, O envoy, to that Pāñcāla, the basest of kings: 'Since you, O evil-minded one, chose a maiden for the sake of my daughter, this very day you shall see the fruit of that arrogance—of this there is no doubt.'"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu tenāsau brāhmaṇo rājasattama dūtaḥ prayāto nagaraṃ dāśārṇanṛpacoditaḥ
english: Thus addressed by him, O best of kings, that brāhmaṇa envoy, urged on by the Dāśārṇa king, set out for the city.

sanskrit: tata āsādayām āsa purodhā drupadaṃ pure tasmai pāñcālako rājā gām arghyaṃ ca susatkṛtam prāpayām āsa rājendra saha tena śikhaṇḍinā
english: Then the chaplain came upon Drupada within the city, and the Pāñcāla king, O lord of kings, offered him a cow and the welcome-water, well honoured, together with Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: tāṃ pūjāṃ nābhyanandat sa vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha yad uktaṃ tena vīreṇa rājñā kāñcanavarmaṇā
english: He did not welcome that homage, but spoke these words, the very words that had been uttered by that heroic king Kāñcanavarman:

sanskrit: yat te 'ham adhamācāra duhitrarthe 'smi vañcitaḥ tasya pāpasya karaṇāt phalaṃ prāpnuhi durmate
english: "Since I, O man of base conduct, have been deceived by you in the matter of my daughter, reap now the fruit of that sin you have wrought, O evil-minded one!"

sanskrit: dehi yuddhaṃ narapate mamādya raṇamūrdhani uddhariṣyāmi te sadyaḥ sāmātyasutabāndhavam
english: "Give me battle, O king, this day at the front of the fray; at once I shall uproot you, together with your counsellors, your sons, and your kinsmen."

sanskrit: tad upālambhasaṃyuktaṃ śrāvitaḥ kila pārthivaḥ daśārṇapatidūtena mantrimadhye purodhasā
english: That speech, fraught with reproach, the king was made to hear, in the midst of his counsellors, from the chaplain who was envoy of the Daśārṇa lord.

sanskrit: abravīd bharataśreṣṭha drupadaḥ praṇayānataḥ yad āha māṃ bhavān brahman saṃbandhivacanād vacaḥ tasyottaraṃ prativaco dūta eva vadiṣyati
english: Then Drupada, O best of the Bharatas, bowing in conciliation, said: "As for the speech your honour, O brāhmaṇa, has spoken to me at the bidding of my kinsman, an envoy of mine shall himself bear the answer in reply to it."

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpreṣayām āsa drupado 'pi mahātmane hiraṇyavarmaṇe dūtaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragam
english: Then Drupada too sent forth to the great-souled Hiraṇyavarman an envoy, a brāhmaṇa who had reached the far shore of the Veda.

sanskrit: samāgamya tu rājñā sa daśārṇapatinā tadā tad vākyam ādade rājan yad uktaṃ drupadena ha
english: Having come into the presence of the king, the lord of the Daśārṇas, he then delivered, O king, the message that had been spoken by Drupada:

sanskrit: āgamaḥ kriyatāṃ vyaktaṃ kumāro vai suto mama mithyaitad uktaṃ kenāpi tan na śraddheyam ity uta
english: "Let an inquiry be made openly: my son is indeed a youth. This has been falsely said by someone; it is not to be believed."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā drupadasya śrutvā; vimarśayukto yuvatīr variṣṭhāḥ saṃpreṣayām āsa sucārurūpāḥ; śikhaṇḍinaṃ strī pumān veti vettum
english: Then that king, having heard Drupada's words, fell to pondering, and sent forth young women of the highest rank, of surpassing beauty, to learn whether Śikhaṇḍin was woman or man.

sanskrit: tāḥ preṣitās tattvabhāvaṃ viditvā; prītyā rājñe tac chaśaṃsur hi sarvam śikhaṇḍinaṃ puruṣaṃ kauravendra; daśārṇarājāya mahānubhāvam
english: Those women, being sent, learned the truth of the matter, and gladly reported it all to the king—that Śikhaṇḍin, O lord of the Kurus, was a man, a mighty soul—to the Dāśārṇa king.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtvā tu rājā sa āgamaṃ prītimān atha saṃbandhinā samāgamya hṛṣṭo vāsam uvāsa ha
english: Then that king, having made the inquiry, was pleased, and meeting with his kinsman, he stayed there in joy and took up his lodging.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍine ca muditaḥ prādād vittaṃ janeśvaraḥ hastino 'śvāṃś ca gāś caiva dāsyo bahuśatās tathā pūjitaś ca pratiyayau nivartya tanayāṃ kila
english: And to Śikhaṇḍin the lord of men, gladdened, gave wealth—elephants and horses and cattle, and many hundreds of female servants—and, having been honoured, he turned back his daughter and departed.

sanskrit: vinītakilbiṣe prīte hemavarmaṇi pārthive pratiyāte tu dāśārṇe hṛṣṭarūpā śikhaṇḍinī
english: When the Dāśārṇa king Hemavarman, his rancour soothed and his heart pleased, had gone back, Śikhaṇḍin was a figure of delight.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya kubero naravāhanaḥ lokānuyātrāṃ kurvāṇaḥ sthūṇasyāgān niveśanam
english: Now after some time Kubera, borne by men, while making his circuit through the worlds, came to the dwelling of Sthūṇa.

sanskrit: sa tadgṛhasyopari vartamāna; ālokayām āsa dhanādhigoptā sthūṇasya yakṣasya niśāmya veśma; svalaṃkṛtaṃ mālyaguṇair vicitram
english: Poised above that house, the guardian of riches looked down, and beheld the dwelling of the yakṣa Sthūṇa, finely adorned and bright with strands of garlands,

sanskrit: lājaiś ca gandhaiś ca tathā vitānair; abhyarcitaṃ dhūpanadhūpitaṃ ca dhvajaiḥ patākābhir alaṃkṛtaṃ ca; bhakṣyānnapeyāmiṣadattahomam
english: honoured with parched grain and perfumes and canopies, made fragrant with incense, decked with standards and banners, and with offerings of food, drink, and flesh laid out in oblation.

sanskrit: tat sthānaṃ tasya dṛṣṭvā tu sarvataḥ samalaṃkṛtam athābravīd yakṣapatis tān yakṣān anugāṃs tadā
english: Seeing his abode thus adorned on every side, the lord of the yakṣas then spoke to those yakṣas, his attendants:

sanskrit: svalaṃkṛtam idaṃ veśma sthūṇasyāmitavikramāḥ nopasarpati māṃ cāpi kasmād adya sumandadhīḥ
english: "Well adorned is this dwelling of Sthūṇa, O you of boundless valour. Yet why does that dull-witted one not approach me today?"

sanskrit: yasmāj jānan sumandātmā mām asau nopasarpati tasmāt tasmai mahādaṇḍo dhāryaḥ syād iti me matiḥ
english: "Since that exceedingly dull-spirited one, though he knows I am here, does not approach me, it is my judgement that a great punishment must be meted out to him."

sanskrit: yakṣā ūcuḥ drupadasya sutā rājan rājño jātā śikhaṇḍinī tasyai nimitte kasmiṃś cit prādāt puruṣalakṣaṇam
english: The yakṣas said: O king, a daughter, Śikhaṇḍinī, was born to King Drupada; and for some reason he gave to her the mark of manhood,

sanskrit: agrahīl lakṣaṇaṃ strīṇāṃ strībhūtas tiṣṭhate gṛhe nopasarpati tenāsau savrīḍaḥ strīsvarūpavān
english: and took in exchange the mark of women; turned female, he stays within the house. For that reason, ashamed and bearing a woman's form, he does not approach.

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇād rājan sthūṇo na tvādya paśyati śrutvā kuru yathānyāyaṃ vimānam iha tiṣṭhatām
english: For this reason, O king, does Sthūṇa not look upon you today. Having heard it, do as is fitting; let your chariot stay here a while.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ānīyatāṃ sthūṇa iti tato yakṣādhipo 'bravīt kartāsmi nigrahaṃ tasyety uvāca sa punaḥ punaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: "Let Sthūṇa be brought," the lord of the yakṣas then said. "I will lay punishment upon him," he declared again and again.

sanskrit: so 'bhyagacchata yakṣendram āhūtaḥ pṛthivīpate strīsvarūpo mahārāja tasthau vrīḍāsamanvitaḥ
english: Summoned, he came before the lord of the yakṣas, O lord of the earth; bearing a woman's form, O great king, he stood overcome with shame.

sanskrit: taṃ śaśāpa susaṃkruddho dhanadaḥ kurunandana evam eva bhavatv asya strītvaṃ pāpasya guhyakāḥ
english: In great wrath the giver of wealth cursed him, O joy of the Kurus: "Even so let the womanhood of this sinful one remain, O guhyakas!"

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd yakṣapatir mahātmā; yasmād adās tv avamanyeha yakṣān śikhaṇḍine lakṣaṇaṃ pāpabuddhe; strīlakṣaṇaṃ cāgrahīḥ pāpakarman
english: Then the great-souled lord of the yakṣas spoke: "Since, scorning the yakṣas here, you gave your mark to Śikhaṇḍin, O evil-minded one, and took the mark of woman, O doer of sin,

sanskrit: apravṛttaṃ sudurbuddhe yasmād etat kṛtaṃ tvayā tasmād adya prabhṛty eva tvaṃ strī sa puruṣas tathā
english: since this unheard-of thing has been done by you, O most foolish one, therefore from this day onward you shall be a woman, and he a man."

sanskrit: tataḥ prasādayām āsur yakṣā vaiśravaṇaṃ kila sthūṇasyārthe kuruṣvāntaṃ śāpasyeti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then the yakṣas sought to appease Vaiśravaṇa for Sthūṇa's sake, saying again and again: "Set a limit to the curse."

sanskrit: tato mahātmā yakṣendraḥ pratyuvācānugāminaḥ sarvān yakṣagaṇāṃs tāta śāpasyāntacikīrṣayā
english: Then the great-souled lord of the yakṣas, my son, replied to all his attendant bands of yakṣas, wishing to set an end to the curse:

sanskrit: hate śikhaṇḍini raṇe svarūpaṃ pratipatsyate sthūṇo yakṣo nirudvego bhavatv iti mahāmanāḥ
english: "When Śikhaṇḍin has been slain in battle, the yakṣa Sthūṇa shall regain his own form," said the high-minded one. "Let him be free of distress."

sanskrit: ity uktvā bhagavān devo yakṣarākṣasapūjitaḥ prayayau saha taiḥ sarvair nimeṣāntaracāribhiḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the blessed god, honoured by yakṣas and rākṣasas, departed together with all those who move in the span between two blinkings of the eye.

sanskrit: sthūṇas tu śāpaṃ saṃprāpya tatraiva nyavasat tadā samaye cāgamat taṃ vai śikhaṇḍī sa kṣapācaram
english: But Sthūṇa, having received the curse, dwelt on there in that place; and at the appointed time Śikhaṇḍin came to him, that wanderer of the night.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamyābravīd vākyaṃ prāpto 'smi bhagavann iti tam abravīt tataḥ sthūṇaḥ prīto 'smīti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Drawing near, he spoke these words: "I have come, O blessed one." Then Sthūṇa said to him, again and again, "I am pleased."

sanskrit: ārjavenāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā rājaputraṃ śikhaṇḍinam sarvam eva yathāvṛttam ācacakṣe śikhaṇḍine
english: Seeing the prince Śikhaṇḍin come in good faith, he told Śikhaṇḍin all that had befallen, just as it had happened.

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca śapto vaiśravaṇenāsmi tvatkṛte pārthivātmaja gacchedānīṃ yathākāmaṃ cara lokān yathāsukham
english: The yakṣa said: I have been cursed by Vaiśravaṇa on your account, O son of a king. Go now, and roam the worlds at your will and your ease.

sanskrit: diṣṭam etat purā manye na śakyam ativartitum gamanaṃ tava ceto hi paulastyasya ca darśanam
english: This, I deem, was ordained of old, and could not be overpassed—your coming, and likewise the visit of Paulastya.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktaḥ śikhaṇḍī tu sthūṇayakṣeṇa bhārata pratyājagāma nagaraṃ harṣeṇa mahatānvitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by the yakṣa Sthūṇa, O Bhārata, Śikhaṇḍin returned to the city filled with great joy.

sanskrit: pūjayām āsa vividhair gandhamālyair mahādhanaiḥ dvijātīn devatāś cāpi caityān atha catuṣpathān
english: With perfumes and garlands of many kinds, and with rich gifts, he honoured the twice-born and the gods, the sanctuaries, and the crossroad shrines.

sanskrit: drupadaḥ saha putreṇa siddhārthena śikhaṇḍinā mudaṃ ca paramāṃ lebhe pāñcālyaḥ saha bāndhavaiḥ
english: And Drupada the Pāñcāla, together with his son Śikhaṇḍin whose purpose was now fulfilled, and with his kinsmen, attained the highest joy.

sanskrit: śiṣyārthaṃ pradadau cāpi droṇāya kurupuṃgava śikhaṇḍinaṃ mahārāja putraṃ strīpūrviṇaṃ tathā
english: And he gave over Śikhaṇḍin as a pupil to Droṇa, O bull of the Kurus—that son, O great king, who had once been a woman.

sanskrit: pratipede catuṣpādaṃ dhanurvedaṃ nṛpātmajaḥ śikhaṇḍī saha yuṣmābhir dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ
english: That prince Śikhaṇḍin received the fourfold science of archery, together with you all, and so did Dhṛṣṭadyumna, son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: mama tv etac carās tāta yathāvat pratyavedayan jaḍāndhabadhirākārā ye yuktā drupade mayā
english: But to me, my son, all this was duly reported by my spies, who, in the guise of dullards, the blind, and the deaf, had been set by me upon Drupada.

sanskrit: evam eṣa mahārāja strīpumān drupadātmajaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ kauravaśreṣṭha śikhaṇḍī rathasattamaḥ
english: Thus, O great king, this son of Drupada, woman-and-man, came into being—Śikhaṇḍin, O best of the Kauravas, the foremost of warriors on the car.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhā kāśipateḥ kanyā ambā nāmeti viśrutā drupadasya kule jātā śikhaṇḍī bharatarṣabha
english: The eldest daughter of the lord of Kāśi, renowned by the name of Ambā, was born in the line of Drupada as Śikhaṇḍin, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: nāham enaṃ dhanuṣpāṇiṃ yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam muhūrtam api paśyeyaṃ prahareyaṃ na cāpy uta
english: Even for a moment I would not look upon him, bow in hand and come forward eager to fight; nor would I strike him.

sanskrit: vratam etan mama sadā pṛthivyām api viśrutam striyāṃ strīpūrvake cāpi strīnāmni strīsvarūpiṇi
english: This vow of mine has ever been famed throughout the earth: that upon a woman, or upon one who was once a woman, one who bears a woman's name or a woman's form,

sanskrit: na muñceyam ahaṃ bāṇān iti kauravanandana na hanyām aham etena kāraṇena śikhaṇḍinam
english: I would never loose my arrows, O joy of the Kurus. For this reason I will not slay Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: etat tattvam ahaṃ veda janma tāta śikhaṇḍinaḥ tato nainaṃ haniṣyāmi samareṣv ātatāyinam
english: I know the truth of Śikhaṇḍin's birth, my son; therefore I will not slay him in battle, even when he comes against me with weapon raised.

sanskrit: yadi bhīṣmaḥ striyaṃ hanyād dhanyād ātmānam apy uta nainaṃ tasmād dhaniṣyāmi dṛṣṭvāpi samare sthitam
english: If Bhīṣma should slay a woman, he would as surely slay his own self. Therefore I will not slay him, even seeing him stand before me in the fray.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etac chrutvā tu kauravyo rājā duryodhanas tadā muhūrtam iva sa dhyātvā bhīṣme yuktam amanyata
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard this, King Duryodhana of the Kuru line then pondered for a moment, and deemed it fitting in Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ punar eva sutas tava madhye sarvasya sainyasya pitāmaham apṛcchata
english: Saṃjaya said: When the night had brightened into dawn, your son once again, in the midst of all the host, questioned the grandsire:

sanskrit: pāṇḍaveyasya gāṅgeya yad etat sainyam uttamam prabhūtanaranāgāśvaṃ mahārathasamākulam
english: "O son of Gaṅgā, this supreme army of the Pāṇḍava, abounding in men and elephants and horses, thronged with great chariot-warriors,

sanskrit: bhīmārjunaprabhṛtibhir maheṣvāsair mahābalaiḥ lokapālopamair guptaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamaiḥ
english: guarded by mighty bowmen of great strength, Bhīma and Arjuna and the rest, peers of the world-guardians, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head—

sanskrit: apradhṛṣyam anāvāryam udvṛttam iva sāgaram senāsāgaram akṣobhyam api devair mahāhave
english: unassailable, irresistible, surging like the swollen ocean, an ocean of an army not to be shaken even by the gods in great battle—

sanskrit: kena kālena gāṅgeya kṣapayethā mahādyute ācāryo vā maheṣvāsaḥ kṛpo vā sumahābalaḥ
english: in what time, O son of Gaṅgā of great splendour, would you destroy it? Or the preceptor, that mighty bowman, or Kṛpa of exceeding strength,

sanskrit: karṇo vā samaraślāghī drauṇir vā dvijasattamaḥ divyāstraviduṣaḥ sarve bhavanto hi bale mama
english: or Karṇa who exults in battle, or Drauṇi, the best of the twice-born? For you are all versed in the divine weapons, and all in my host."

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ jñātuṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me hṛdi nityaṃ mahābāho vaktum arhasi tan mama
english: "This I wish to know, for a great curiosity dwells ever in my heart, O mighty-armed one; it behoves you to tell it to me."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca anurūpaṃ kuruśreṣṭha tvayy etat pṛthivīpate balābalam amitrāṇāṃ sveṣāṃ ca yadi pṛcchasi
english: Bhīṣma said: This befits you, O best of the Kurus, O lord of the earth—if you ask of the strength and weakness of your foes and of your own.

sanskrit: śṛṇu rājan mama raṇe yā śaktiḥ paramā bhavet astravīryaṃ raṇe yac ca bhujayoś ca mahābhuja
english: Hear, O king, what my utmost power in battle would be, and the might of my weapons in the fray, and the strength of my two arms, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: ārjavenaiva yuddhena yoddhavya itaro janaḥ māyāyuddhena māyāvī ity etad dharmaniścayaḥ
english: The honest foe is to be fought by open battle, the wielder of illusion by battle of illusion—such is the settled rule of dharma.

sanskrit: hanyām ahaṃ mahābāho pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm divase divase kṛtvā bhāgaṃ prāgāhnikaṃ mama
english: I would slay, O mighty-armed one, the army of the Pāṇḍavas day by day, setting myself a forenoon's portion each day.

sanskrit: yodhānāṃ daśasāhasraṃ kṛtvā bhāgaṃ mahādyute sahasraṃ rathinām ekam eṣa bhāgo mato mama
english: Ten thousand warriors, O greatly resplendent one, set as my portion, and one thousand chariot-fighters besides—this is the share I reckon mine.

sanskrit: anenāhaṃ vidhānena saṃnaddhaḥ satatotthitaḥ kṣapayeyaṃ mahat sainyaṃ kālenānena bhārata
english: By this measure, armed and ever ready, I would destroy that great army in the span of such a time, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yadi tv astrāṇi muñceyaṃ mahānti samare sthitaḥ śatasāhasraghātīni hanyāṃ māsena bhārata
english: But if, standing in the battle, I should loose the great weapons that slay by hundreds of thousands, I would make an end within a month, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śrutvā bhīṣmasya tad vākyaṃ rājā duryodhanas tadā paryapṛcchata rājendra droṇam aṅgirasāṃ varam
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard those words of Bhīṣma, King Duryodhana then, O lord of kings, put his question to Droṇa, the best of the Aṅgirasas:

sanskrit: ācārya kena kālena pāṇḍuputrasya sainikān nihanyā iti taṃ droṇaḥ pratyuvāca hasann iva
english: "O preceptor, in what time would you slay the soldiers of the son of Pāṇḍu?" To him Droṇa, as though with a smile, made answer:

sanskrit: sthaviro 'smi kuruśreṣṭha mandaprāṇaviceṣṭitaḥ astrāgninā nirdaheyaṃ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: "I am old, O best of the Kurus, slow now in breath and action; yet with the fire of my weapons I would burn up the army of the Pāṇḍavas,

sanskrit: yathā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo māseneti matir mama eṣā me paramā śaktir etan me paramaṃ balam
english: in a month, even as Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu has said—such is my judgement. This is my utmost power, this my utmost strength."

sanskrit: dvābhyām eva tu māsābhyāṃ kṛpaḥ śāradvato 'bravīt drauṇis tu daśarātreṇa pratijajñe balakṣayam karṇas tu pañcarātreṇa pratijajñe mahāstravit
english: Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat said: "In two months only." But Drauṇi pledged the destruction of the host in ten nights; and Karṇa, the knower of the great weapons, pledged it in five.
